title: Marketplace Security Questionnaire Responses (Draft) — AWS/GCP Marketplace
content:
Audience: AWS Marketplace + GCP Marketplace security reviewers and customer security questionnaire workflows (procurement-led).

Status: Draft response bank. Some answers reference evidence that is “available under NDA” (see Evidence Stubs section). Avoid promising features not GA.

Owner for external sends: Security (Naomi Feldman) + GRC (Olga Petrov)
Routing: security@redwoodinference.com (external) / #eng-security (internal)

Internal references (Confluence):
- Marketplace Security Documentation Pack (index): sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/compliance-evidence/marketplace-security-documentation-pack.json
- Data Handling + Retention (Marketplace): sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/data-residency-and-retention/marketplace-data-handling-and-retention.json
- Audit Logs (Marketplace customers): sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/audit-logging/audit-logs-for-marketplace-customers.json

========================
1) COMPANY + COMPLIANCE POSTURE
========================

Q: Do you maintain a formal information security program?
A: Yes. Redwood Inference maintains a formal information security program with documented policies and standards covering access control, encryption, incident response, vulnerability management, change management, logging/monitoring, vendor risk management, and business continuity. Security is governed by an executive sponsor (Dr. Aisha Rahman) with dedicated Security Engineering and GRC teams.
Evidence pointer: “Marketplace Security Documentation Pack” index (Confluence) + policy excerpts available under NDA.

Q: Are you SOC 2 audited? What type and scope?
A: Redwood Inference maintains a SOC 2 Type II program. The report is available under NDA and includes controls relevant to security, availability, and confidentiality aligned to our production systems supporting the Redwood API and customer control plane.
Notes/guardrails: Share report only via approved channel (NDA + secure portal).
Evidence stub: SOC 2 Type II report PDF + bridge letter (if requested).

Q: Are you ISO 27001 certified?
A: Redwood Inference’s security controls are aligned with ISO 27001/27002 practices; certification status and certificates (if applicable for a specific scope) are shared under NDA as part of the evidence packet.
Evidence stub: ISO certificate / Statement of Applicability (SOA) (under NDA if applicable).

Q: Do you undergo third-party penetration tests?
A: Yes. Redwood conducts periodic third-party penetration testing of relevant surfaces (e.g., web console and APIs) and remediates findings according to severity-based SLAs.
Evidence stub: Executive summary of latest pen test (redacted) + remediation attestation.

Q: Do you have a bug bounty program?
A: Redwood operates a coordinated vulnerability disclosure process. Bug bounty participation (if enabled for a given surface) can be discussed and confirmed under NDA.
Evidence stub: VDP / disclosure process description.

========================
2) SERVICE DESCRIPTION + SHARED RESPONSIBILITY
========================

Q: Describe the service being purchased through AWS/GCP Marketplace.
A: Marketplace listings correspond to Redwood Inference’s LLM inference platform offerings:
- Hosted API: managed inference endpoints accessible via Redwood API (REST/SDK).
- Dedicated: reserved GPU capacity with isolation and predictable throughput.
- Private: VPC and/or on-prem deployment options for regulated workloads.
Marketplace buyers subscribe via AWS/GCP Marketplace; Redwood provisions entitlements into a Redwood organization in our console.
Evidence pointer: Marketplace PRD overview for procurement flow (internal): sources/confluence/product-docs/requirements/cloud-marketplace-listing-refresh-prd.json

Q: What is the shared responsibility model?
A: Redwood is responsible for the security of the Redwood service components we operate (control plane, managed inference runtime for Hosted/Dedicated where applicable, security monitoring, patching, access controls, logging, and incident response). Customers are responsible for:
- Securing their Redwood credentials/API keys and user access.
- Configuring SSO, IP allowlists, and retention settings where available.
- Ensuring prompts/inputs comply with their internal policies and applicable regulations.
- Application-layer security in their own environment.
For Private (VPC/on-prem), responsibilities are further split based on who operates the underlying compute/networking; Redwood provides deployment guidance and security configuration recommendations.
Evidence pointer: Marketplace Security Documentation Pack (Shared Responsibility section).

========================
3) DATA HANDLING, PRIVACY, RETENTION, RESIDENCY
========================

Q: What customer data do you process?
A: Redwood processes customer-provided inputs to run inference (prompts/messages and optional files/structured content, depending on API usage) and returns model outputs. Redwood also processes operational metadata required to operate and secure the service (request IDs, timestamps, org/project IDs, usage metrics, and error logs). Data categories and defaults are documented in the marketplace data handling reference.
Evidence pointer: sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/data-residency-and-retention/marketplace-data-handling-and-retention.json

Q: Do you use customer prompts/outputs to train models?
A: By default, Redwood does not use customer prompts/outputs to train foundation models. Any optional product-improvement uses (if offered) are governed by contract terms and customer configuration.
Notes: Keep wording consistent with marketplace listing + contractual terms. Do not imply “never” unless contract guarantees are in place.
Evidence pointer: Marketplace Security Documentation Pack (Data Use section).

Q: What is the default retention for prompts/outputs and logs?
A: Redwood maintains retention controls appropriate for production operations and security monitoring. Default retention periods and configurable options (where applicable) are documented for marketplace buyers.
Evidence pointer: sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/data-residency-and-retention/marketplace-data-handling-and-retention.json

Q: Can customers request deletion of data?
A: Redwood supports data deletion requests subject to contractual scope, legal obligations, and technical feasibility. Deletion workflows and response timelines are handled through support and security channels.
Evidence stub: Data deletion process + support ticket workflow.

Q: Where is data stored and processed? (Data residency)
A: Data residency depends on the deployment mode and configured region(s). Redwood supports regional processing for marketplace customers aligned to our available cloud regions, with specifics captured in the data residency and retention reference.
Evidence pointer: sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/data-residency-and-retention/marketplace-data-handling-and-retention.json

Q: Do you support customer-managed keys (CMK/KMS/HSM)?
A: Redwood supports encryption using cloud KMS in supported deployments and offers key management integrations appropriate for enterprise workloads. For Private deployments, customer-managed key integrations can be configured within the customer environment.
Notes: Provide exact capability by product tier/deployment (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) during questionnaire completion.
Evidence pointer: Marketplace Security Documentation Pack (Encryption + Key Management section).

========================
4) ENCRYPTION
========================

Q: Is data encrypted in transit?
A: Yes. Data in transit is protected using TLS on external-facing endpoints and service-to-service communication paths where applicable.
Evidence stub: Architecture diagram + TLS configuration standards (under NDA).

Q: Is data encrypted at rest?
A: Yes. Redwood uses encryption at rest for production data stores and logs where applicable, using industry-standard encryption mechanisms and cloud provider primitives.
Evidence pointer: Marketplace Security Documentation Pack (Encryption section).

Q: How are secrets stored and rotated?
A: Secrets are stored in managed secrets systems with restricted access and audited retrieval. Rotation practices are implemented for sensitive credentials according to policy and risk profile.
Evidence stub: Secrets management policy excerpt + rotation schedule overview.

========================
5) ACCESS CONTROL + AUTHN/AUTHZ
========================

Q: Do you support SSO/SAML?
A: Redwood supports enterprise authentication options (including SSO) for organizations where enabled per plan/contract.
Notes: Confirm whether the customer is buying Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private and whether SSO is included in their SKU/add-on.
Evidence stub: Console admin guide excerpt + SSO configuration screenshots (redacted).

Q: How is least privilege enforced internally?
A: Redwood enforces least-privilege access controls via role-based access control (RBAC), production access approval workflows, and periodic access reviews. Administrative actions are logged.
Evidence pointer: Marketplace Security Documentation Pack (Access Control section).

Q: Do you conduct access reviews?
A: Yes. Redwood performs periodic access reviews for privileged access and maintains records as part of our compliance program.
Evidence stub: Access review evidence screenshots (redacted) + SOC 2 control mapping.

========================
6) AUDIT LOGGING + MONITORING
========================

Q: Do you provide audit logs to customers?
A: Yes. Redwood provides audit logging for key administrative and security-relevant events (e.g., user/admin actions, org/project changes, credential/API key events) and supports access to these logs for enterprise workflows.
Evidence pointer: sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/audit-logging/audit-logs-for-marketplace-customers.json

Q: What events are logged, and how long are audit logs retained?
A: Logged event types and retention are documented for marketplace customers, including available export/integration options for SIEM.
Evidence pointer: sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/audit-logging/audit-logs-for-marketplace-customers.json

Q: Do you monitor for security events and anomalous activity?
A: Yes. Redwood uses monitoring and alerting for security-relevant signals (e.g., authentication anomalies, elevated error rates, suspicious administrative actions) and on-call workflows for incident response.
Evidence stub: Monitoring/alerting overview + incident response runbook (redacted).

========================
7) VULNERABILITY MANAGEMENT + PATCHING
========================

Q: How do you manage vulnerabilities?
A: Redwood runs a vulnerability management program including asset inventory, vulnerability scanning, dependency management, and remediation SLAs based on severity. Critical security issues are prioritized and tracked to closure.
Evidence stub: Vulnerability management policy excerpt + sample remediation ticket screenshots (redacted).

Q: Do you scan container images / dependencies?
A: Yes. Redwood scans dependencies and build artifacts as part of CI/CD security controls, and blocks/alerts on known critical issues per policy.
Evidence stub: CI/CD security control summary.

========================
8) SDLC + CHANGE MANAGEMENT
========================

Q: Do you have secure SDLC practices?
A: Yes. Redwood applies secure SDLC practices including code review, automated testing, CI/CD controls, and separation of environments. Sensitive changes require additional review/approvals.
Evidence stub: SDLC control summary + sample PR review checklist excerpt.

Q: Do you perform security reviews for material changes?
A: Yes. Security reviews are performed for changes impacting authentication, authorization, data handling, encryption, and external-facing endpoints.
Evidence stub: Security review template + example (redacted).

========================
9) INCIDENT RESPONSE + BREACH NOTIFICATION
========================

Q: Do you have an incident response plan?
A: Yes. Redwood maintains an incident response plan with defined severity levels, roles/responsibilities, escalation, communications, and post-incident review.
Evidence stub: IR plan (redacted) + on-call process description.

Q: What is your breach notification timeline?
A: Redwood follows contractual breach notification terms and applicable legal requirements. Specific timelines are finalized in customer agreements / marketplace private offers where applicable.
Notes: Avoid hard-coding hours/days here unless confirmed by Legal (Michael Grant / Sofia Mendes).
Evidence stub: Contractual template language (Legal-provided).

========================
10) BUSINESS CONTINUITY / DISASTER RECOVERY
========================

Q: Do you have BCP/DR procedures?
A: Yes. Redwood maintains business continuity and disaster recovery procedures appropriate to the services provided, including backup practices and recovery objectives that are reviewed as part of our compliance program.
Evidence stub: BCP/DR summary (redacted) + test evidence (tabletop or failover test).

========================
11) SUBPROCESSORS + VENDOR RISK
========================

Q: Do you use subprocessors?
A: Redwood uses subprocessors to deliver the service (e.g., cloud infrastructure providers). Subprocessor disclosures and updates are handled through our standard documentation and customer notifications as contractually required.
Evidence stub: Subprocessor list + vendor risk summary (redacted).

========================
12) MARKETPLACE-SPECIFIC (AWS/GCP)
========================

Q: How does marketplace entitlement/provisioning work, and is it secure?
A: Marketplace buyers subscribe via AWS/GCP Marketplace, then validate entitlement during Redwood org provisioning. Entitlements are verified via marketplace integration endpoints and synchronized into Redwood systems with least-privilege IAM/service credentials. Errors (e.g., propagation delay) are handled with retry logic and clear user guidance.
Evidence pointer (engineering): entitlement verification and sync hardening work tracked internally (see ENG-22110, ENG-22116) and console onboarding entrypoint (ENG-22112).

Q: How is usage metered for marketplace billing?
A: Marketplace SKUs map to defined billing dimensions/metering identifiers aligned with internal usage meters (e.g., token usage for Hosted, capacity reservation dimensions for Dedicated, and platform fees/support for Private where applicable). Metering identifiers are maintained in our billing catalog to ensure correct reconciliation.
Notes: Provide SKU-to-dimension mapping separately (do not embed confidential pricing in security response).

Q: Do you support private offers and custom terms?
A: Yes, for enterprise procurement. Private offers may include custom SLAs, security add-ons, and billing dimensions; all security claims remain consistent with the baseline security packet.

========================
13) PRODUCT MODE DIFFERENCES (IMPORTANT FOR QUESTIONNAIRES)
========================

When answering, clarify which product mode applies:
- Hosted API: Redwood-managed runtime and control plane.
- Dedicated: reserved capacity with stronger isolation; still Redwood-managed in most cases.
- Private: customer environment constraints; security responsibilities and evidence differ.

If a question asks “Where is the data stored?” or “Who can access data?”, always specify:
- environment (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)
- region(s)
- retention configuration
- whether customer-managed keys are in use

========================
14) EVIDENCE STUBS (PLACEHOLDERS)
========================

(These are not attached to this Drive doc; share via approved secure channel once NDA is in place.)
- SOC 2 Type II report (PDF) + bridge letter (if between audit periods)
- ISO certificate + Statement of Applicability (if applicable)
- Pen test report executive summary (redacted) + remediation statement
- Vulnerability management policy excerpt + sample remediation evidence (redacted)
- Incident response plan (redacted) + tabletop/test record
- BCP/DR summary (redacted) + test record
- Architecture/data flow diagram for marketplace onboarding + entitlement verification
- Audit log feature documentation (customer-facing) + screenshots (redacted)
